learning_objective: 📊 Understand the root cause of all economic problems (scarcity) and discover why statistics is the ultimate tool for making sense of the real world!

उत्पादन (संसाधनों को उपयोगी वस्तुओं में बदलना)
मात्रात्मक आंकड़े (जिन्हें संख्याओं में मापा जा सके)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Economics exists because of 'Scarcity'. Human wants are unlimited, but the resources (money, time, land) to satisfy them are limited and have alternative uses. We study economics to make the best possible choices.

Economics studies three main activities: Consumption (consumers buying goods for satisfaction), Production (producers making goods for profit), and Distribution (how income is shared among land, labor, capital, and enterprise).

In a plural sense, statistics means numerical facts systematically collected (data). In a singular sense, it refers to the science of collecting, organizing, presenting, analyzing, and interpreting numerical data.
It simplifies complex data, helps in comparing facts, studying relationships (like price and demand), formulating government policies, and economic forecasting.

Statistics only deals with quantitative data (not beauty or honesty), it only studies groups/aggregates (not a single person's income), and data can be easily manipulated or misused if not handled by experts.

fun_activity.title: 🛍️ The Scarcity Game
fun_activity.instructions: Imagine you have exactly ₹500. Write down everything you want to buy right now. Add up the total cost. Is it more than ₹500? That's scarcity! Now, strike out items until your total is under ₹500. You just made an 'Economic Choice'!

exam_tips: 📌 Always mention that 'Statistics studies aggregates of facts'. A single isolated number (like Ram's height is 5 ft) is NOT statistics because it cannot be compared.
📌 Distinguish clearly between the singular sense (statistical methods) and plural sense (numerical data).
📌 Scarcity is the mother of all economic problems. No scarcity = no need for economics.
quick_recap: ⭐ Alfred Marshall defined Economics as the 'study of mankind in the ordinary business of life'.
⭐ Economic policies (like taxation, poverty alleviation) heavily rely on accurate statistical data.
⭐ Qualitative attributes (like intelligence or gender) cannot be studied directly in statistics unless they are converted into numerical scores.
